newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds wrapped up for Christmas.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds wrapped up for Christmas.

text.p: *Australian bonds had a fairly uneventful shortened session ahead of the two-day Christmas holiday with yields off slightly.
*Market now closed until 8.30 a.m. (2130 GMT) on Friday.
Australian bonds had a fairly uneventful shortened session ahead of the two-day Christmas holiday with yields off slightly, which was purely a reflection of a firm U.S. Treasury market on Thursday.

Futures floor trading finished at 12.30 p.m. (0130 GMT) and the market resumes through screen-based SYCOM on Friday at 8.30 a.m. (2130 GMT), while physical activity is expected to be limited. There is no afterhours trading in the meantime.
Local November motor registrations rose a stronger than expected 6.3 percent, but this failed to stir the market which was content to mark time ahead of the holiday.
U.S. Treasuries gained ground on Thursday after the University of Michigan consumer index for December fell to 96.2 from 99.2 in November when analysts had expected it to hold around the 99 level.
However, U.S. yields edged up slightly in Tokyo trading.

Turnover in local futures contracts was extremely thin with just under a 2,000 lots recorded on the December 10-year bond futures contract, which see-sawed around the psychological 92.500 level for most of the session after support held at 92.450 in afterhours trading.

Spread differentials to other dollar bloc bonds were fairly mixed, although the local long-end kept pretty much in tune with movements in U.S. Treasuries. Resistance remains at 110 basis points on the Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread.
